references.text: God promises to bless those who bless Abraham and curse those who curse him, reflecting the promise to be an enemy against Israel's enemies.
Moses promises that if Israel obeys the Lord's voice and keeps His commandments, all blessings will come upon them.
The Lord promises to place all curses on Israel's enemies and on those who hate and persecute them.
God promises Abraham that his offspring will take possession of their enemies' gates as a result of obedience.
Isaiah conveys that if the people are willing and obedient, they shall eat the good things of the land.
Jeremiah repeats the covenant formula about listening to God's voice: then He will be their God and they will be His people.
God promises that if Israel obeys His voice and keeps His covenant, they shall be His treasured possession and a kingdom of priests.
Moses promises that if Israel keeps all the commandments and loves the Lord, God will drive out all the nations before them.
Paul quotes God's word that vengeance belongs to Him and He will repay, linking it to God's promise to be an enemy against His people's enemies.
Direct theological mirror image: 1 Sam 12:15 confirms the consequence of breaking the same covenant conditions for which Exodus 23:22 promises reward.
The same covenant formula ('listen to my voice') connects identity (19:5) and protection/warfare (23:22) as two sides of the promise of obedience.
Psalm 18:41 is a concrete experience/fulfillment of the promise in Exodus 23:22 that God will be an enemy against your enemies.
Clear theological contrast: God's warfare against enemies (Ex) versus Jesus' command to love enemies (Luke), illuminating the development in God's plan.
The same covenant formula ('hear the Lord's voice') links the promise of protection (Ex) with the requirement for righteous action (Deut).
